qs.q:
According to Whittaker's classification, how many of the following characteristics are present in both Kingdom Plantae and Fungi?
(I) Eukaryotic, generally multicellular.
(II) Heterotrophic mode of nutrition.
(III) Polysaccharide cell wall.
(IV) True tissue present, and both asexual and sexual reproduction occur.
(V) Well-developed nucleus and other organelles.
(VI) Presence of chloroplast.
qs.s: I, III, IV, V are correct features shared by both Kingdom Plantae and Fungi. Fungi do not possess chloroplasts and plants are autotrophs.

qs.q: Which of the following statements about mycoplasma is wrong?
qs.s: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall, making them insensitive to penicillin which acts on cell wall synthesis.

qs.q:
How many of the following list of organisms lacks cellulosic cell wall
Diatoms, Cyanobacteria, Chlorella,
Chlamydomonas, Spirogyra, Nostoc,
Anabaena, Archaea, Eubacteria,
Dinoflagellates, Gonyaulax,
Spores of Slime moulds
qs.s: Diatoms, Cyanobacteria, Nostoc, Anabaena, Archaea, and Eubacteria lack a cellulosic cell wall.

qs.q: A dikaryon is formed when
o: The two haploid cells do not fuse immediately
qs.s: A dikaryon (n + n) condition occurs when fusion of two haploid cells is delayed during plasmogamy.

qs.q: Which of the following statement about plant is false?
o: Plants show alternation of generations during their life cycle
qs.s: Plants are non-motile (immotile) organisms.

qs.q:
Select from the following the total number of features belonging to animal kingdom.
1. Multicellular, heterotrophic.
2. Most of them capable of locomotion.
3. Have definite shape and size.
4. Digestion of food in internal cavity.
5. Holozoic mode of nutrition.
6. Stored food reserve as glycogen or fat.
7. Higher forms shows sensory and neuromotor mechanism.
8. Some members are autotrophic.
9. Presence of cellulose cell wall..
10. Sexual reproduction generally by copulation of male and female followed by embryological development
qs.s: Eight features (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10) belong to Kingdom Animalia, while presence of cellulose cell wall and autotrophic nutrition do not.

qs.q: How many of the given organisms are obligate parasites which take over the machinery of the host cell? TMV, Nostoc, Bacteriophage, HIV, Oscillatoria
qs.s: TMV, Bacteriophage, and HIV are viruses, which are obligate intracellular parasites.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is wrong for viroids?
o: Their RNA is of high molecular weight.
qs.s: Viroids consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and lack a protein coat.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat.
Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins.
qs.s: The infectious constituent in viruses is their genetic material (DNA or RNA), not the protein coat.

qs.q: Find out the correct statement.
o: In lichens, the algal component is called phycobiont and fungal component is known as mycobiont, which are heterotrophic and autotrophic respectively.
Viroid contains RNA of low molecular weight and protein coat
A virus contains both RNA and DNA
qs.s: Viruses cannot replicate independently and are mandatory (obligatory) intracellular parasites.

qs.q:
Find the correct statements from the following:
(I) According to the five-kingdom classification of R.H. Whittaker, producers are placed in Monera, Protista, and Plantae,
(II) In Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, eukaryotes are assigned to all five kingdoms.
(III) Saccharomyces is unicellular and useful in fermentation.
(IV) According to the three-domain theory, two domains include prokaryotic organisms.
(V) Euglenoids have two flagella, one lies longitudinally and the other transversely.
(VI) Slime mould spores are dispersed by air currents.
qs.s: Statements I, III, IV, and VI are correct. Eukaryotes are assigned to four kingdoms (excluding Monera), and dinoflagellates have longitudinal/transverse flagella.

qs.q:
Consider the organisms mentioned and select the number of heterotrophs
Green sulphur bacteria, Purple sulphur bacteria, Iron bacteria, Sulphur bacteria, Frankia, Nostoc, Rhizobium, Vibrio
qs.s: Rhizobium, Frankia, and Vibrio are heterotrophic organisms.

qs.q: Which pair of the following belongs to Basidiomycetes?
qs.s: Bird's nest fungi (Cyathus) and puffballs (Lycoperdon) belong to class Basidiomycetes.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy.
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile on non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy.
Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes.
Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells.
qs.s: Plasmogamy is the fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes.

qs.q:
Match the following classes of Fungi (Column-I) with the examples (Column-II).
Choose the correct option:
A. Phycomycetes
B. Ascomycetes
C. Basidiomycetes
D. Deuteromycetes

P. Penicillium
Q. Alternaria
R. Albugo
S. Puccinia
qs.s: Albugo is a phycomycete, Penicillium is an ascomycete, Puccinia is a basidiomycete, and Alternaria is a deuteromycete.

qs.q:
How many statements are correct for truffles and moreis?
i. They have septate monokaryotic mycelium
ii. Reproduce asexually by nonmotile endogenous spores
iii. Produce haploid exogenous sexual spores arranged in an orderly manner
iv. Their fruiting bodies are edible
qs.s: Morels and truffles are edible ascomycetes with haploid endogenously produced ascospores in asci within ascocarps.

qs.q: An association between roots of higher plants and fungi is called
qs.s: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between fungi and the roots of higher plants.

qs.q:
Difference between virus and viroid is
(I) Absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus.
(II) Presence of low molecular weight RNA in virus but absent in viroid.
(III) Some viruses have RNA as genetic material and viroids also have RNA as their genetic material.
qs.s: Viroids lack a protein coat unlike viruses, and both contain RNA as genetic material.

qs.q:
What is common in Ustilago, Neurospora, and Agaricus?
(I) All have a dikaryotic phase in their life cycle.
(II) All produce motile sexual spores.
(III) All are edible.
(IV) The mycelium is branched and septate.
qs.s: All three have a dikaryotic phase and a branched, septate mycelium.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about slime moulds.
I. Slime moulds are saprophytic protists
II. The spores possess true walls
Which of the statements(s) given above is/are correct?
o: I is true, But II is false
Both I and II are false
I is false but II is true
Both I and II are true
qs.s: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists, and their spores possess true resistant cellulosic cell walls.

qs.q: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by
qs.s: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification in 1969.

qs.q:
The following features represent which group of organisms?
(I) Microscopic
(II) Chief producers in oceans
(III) Found in fresh water as well as in marine environments, planktons.
(IV) Indestructible cell wall
(V) The walls are embedded with silica, making them indestructible.
qs.s: Diatoms are microscopic, oceanic chief producers with indestructible silica-embedded cell walls.

qs.q: Curing of tea leaves is brought about by the activity of
qs.s: Curing of tea leaves to enhance flavor is carried out by bacteria such as Micrococcus candidans.

qs.q: Which of the following are likely to be present in deep sea water?
qs.s: Archaebacteria are adapted to extreme environmental conditions including deep sea hydrothermal vents.

qs.q: Slime moulds - Under P conditions, they form an R called Q which may grow and spread over several feet. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. In the above mentioned incomplete statement, labeling represents
o: P-Aggregation, Q- Plasmodium, R - Suitable condition
qs.s: Under suitable conditions, slime moulds form an aggregation called Plasmodium.

qs.q:
State whether the given statements are true or false.
I. Bacteria are simple in structure, but complex in behaviour
II. Some of the bacteria are autotrophic. They may be photosynthetic autotrophic or chemosynthetic autotrophic.
III. Heterotrophic nutrition involves obtaining nutrition either through parasitism or saprotrophism
o: I is true, II and II are false
I, II and III are true
qs.s: All three given statements about bacterial structure and nutritional modes are correct.

qs.q:
The following characteristics are of which of the given fungi?
A. Sex organs are absent but plasmogamy is by fusion of two somatic cells of different strains or genotype.
B. Asexual spores are generally not found.
qs.s: Basidiomycetes lack sex organs and generally do not produce asexual spores; plasmogamy occurs by somatogamy.

qs.q: Read the following statements and select the incorrect statement.
o: The cyanobacteria is an autrophic bacteria
The cyanobacteria are unicellular, colonial or filamentous, freshwater/ marine or terrestrial algae.
Mucor belongs to class phycomycetes of kingdom fungi
qs.s: Bacteria exhibit vast metabolic diversity; they can be autotrophic, parasitic, or saprophytic.

qs.q:
Study the following statements and identify the correct option given below.
I. Viruses that infect plants have single-stranded RNA and viruses that infect animals have either single or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA
II. Bacterial viruses or Bacteriophages are usually single-stranded RNA viruses.
o: I is true, but II is false
I is false, but II is true
qs.s: Bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses, making statement II false.

qs.q: Choose the correct statement.
o: The cell wall is present in all monerans
The cell wall is present in all protistans
The cell wall is present in all the members of Plantae
qs.s: All members of Kingdom Plantae possess a eukaryotic cellulosic cell wall.

qs.q: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy is a disease caused by prions in a:
qs.s: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), or mad cow disease, is a prion disease affecting cattle.

qs.q: Choose the incorrect statement about members of kingdom-monera
o: All of them live in or on other organisms as parasites
Some synthesise their own food from inorganic solutes
Bacterial structure is very simple, they are very complex in behaviour.
Hundreds of bacteria are present in handful of soil
qs.s: Not all monerans are parasites; many are free-living autotrophs or saprophytes.

qs.q: Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria in:
qs.s: Archaebacteria have a unique cell wall structure lacking peptidoglycan, which enables them to survive extreme conditions.

qs.q: Association between Mycobiont and Phycobiont are found in
qs.s: Lichens represent a symbiotic association between a phycobiont (alga) and a mycobiont (fungus).

qs.q: A student while extracting DNA from Aspergillus fungus requires break open the cell wall. Name the enzyme used for the process?
qs.s: Fungal cell walls contain chitin, which is degraded using the enzyme chitinase.

qs.q: True nucleus is absent in:
qs.s: Anabaena is a prokaryotic cyanobacterium and lacks a true membrane-bound nucleus.

qs.q: Some hypothermophilic organisms that grow in highly acidic (pH 2) habitats belong to the 2 groups
qs.s: Thermoacidophiles belong to Archaea, though some extremophilic Eubacteria also inhabit high-temperature acidic environments.

qs.q: Which of the following shows coiled RNA strand and capsomeres?
qs.s: Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) has helical symmetry with a coiled single-stranded RNA wrapped in capsomeres.

qs.q:
The following features belong to class
A. Members are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants
B. Fusion of gametes may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
C. Mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.
D. Spores are endogenously produced in sporangium.
E. Asexual reproduction by zoospores or aplanospores.
qs.s: Coenocytic, aseptate mycelium and endogenous spores in sporangia are key characteristics of Phycomycetes.

qs.q:
Study the given properties. Which one option has all the properties found in all organisms of the five-kingdom classification?
(I) Presence of a cell membrane
(II) Cell wall present
(III) Autotrophic nutrition
(IV) Chemosynthetic nutrition
(V) Cellular respiration
qs.s: All living organisms across the five kingdoms possess a plasma membrane and perform cellular respiration.

qs.q: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
qs.s: Saccharomyces (yeast) is a eukaryotic unicellular fungus.

qs.q: Select the wrong statement
o: W.M. Stanley showed that viruses could be crystallised.
The viroids were discovered by D.J. Ivanowsky.
Mosaic disease in tobacco and AIDS in human being are caused by viruses.
The term 'contagium vivum fluidum' was coined by Beijerinck.
qs.s: Viroids were discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971, not by D.J. Ivanowsky.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions
N₂ fixing bacteria pick up free N₂ from soil atmosphere and convert it into nitrogenous compounds.
Pathogenic bacteria cause 90% of human diseases
qs.s: Mycoplasma are facultative anaerobes and can survive without oxygen.

qs.q: Which of the following components provide sticky character to the bacterial cell ?
qs.s: Glycocalyx forms a sticky, gummy capsule or slime layer surrounding the cell wall of bacteria.

qs.q:
Find the correct statement from the following
(I) Linnaeus's Kingdom system of classification includes Plantae and Animalia.
(II) Dinoflagellates - Water bloom.
(III) Golden algae - Chief producer in the ocean.
(IV) Mycoplasma - Smallest cell.
(V) "Drosophila of the plant kingdom" Claviceps.
(VI) In lichen, the algal component is known as mycobiont and the fungal component as phycobiont.
qs.s: Statements I, III, and IV are correct. Neurospora is the Drosophila of plant kingdom, and algal component is phycobiont.

qs.q: The motile bacteria are able to move by
qs.s: Flagella made of flagellin protein are responsible for motility in bacteria.

qs.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
TMV virus - ssRNA - Mosaic disease
Zoospore - Asexual spore - Phycomycetes
Plasmodium - Sporozoan Malaria
Rust fungi Puccinia - Basidiomycetes
Conidia - Sexual spore - Ascospore
qs.s: Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct. Conidia are asexual spores, whereas ascospores are sexual spores.

qs.q:
How many statements features are correct for bacteriophage?
i. They have polygonal head and envelope
ii. Contractile tail sheath present
iii. Tail fibres are absent
iv. Nucleic acid as double stranded circular DNA usually
qs.s: Bacteriophages possess tail fibers that aid in attachment to host bacterial cells.

qs.q: A bacterium is capable of withstanding extreme heat, dryness and toxic chemicals. This indicates that it is probably able to form:
qs.s: Endospores produced by bacteria like Bacillus are highly resistant to heat, desiccation, and chemicals.

qs.q: Which one of the following organism is not an eukaryote?
qs.s: Escherichia coli is a Gram-negative prokaryotic bacterium.

qs.q:
Which of the following is true regarding Mycoplasma?
(I) They do not have a cell wall.
(II) They produce a cell wall made up peptidoglycan.
(III) They can survive without oxygen.
(IV) They can cause diseases in animals and plants.
qs.s: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall completely, can survive anaerobically, and cause plant and animal diseases.

qs.q:
How many organisms in the list given below are autotrophs?
Mucor, Albugo, Penicillium, Lactobacillus, Nostoc, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, Streptomyces, Saccharomyces, Trypanosoma, Porphyra
qs.s: Nostoc, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, and Porphyra are autotrophic.

qs.q: Cell wall is absent in
qs.s: Mycoplasma are completely wall-less microorganisms.

qs.q: Which of the statements given below is incorrect?
o: Biological classification is the scientific ordering of organisms in a hierarchial series of groups on the basis of their relationships, i.e. morphological, evolutionary and other
Whittaker classified organisms on the basis of autotrophic and heterotrophic mode of nutrition
In five kingdom system of classification, living organisms can be divided into prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells on the basis of cell structure
Mycoplasma is the smallest acellular living organism
qs.s: Mycoplasma is a cellular living organism, not acellular.

qs.q:
Among the following how many of them belong to Phycomycetes.
I. Mucor
II. Albugo
III. Claviceps
IV. Agaricus
V. Puffballs
qs.s: Mucor and Albugo belong to class Phycomycetes.

qs.q: Identify the algae known for a biological activity called bioluminescence.
qs.s: Noctiluca is a marine dinoflagellate famous for bioluminescence, producing light in sea water.

qs.q: Read the following statement (a) Monera reproduce only sexually (b) Cyanobacteria are oxygenic (c) Monerans have a true nucleus (d) Monerans include unicellular eukaryotic organism Choose the correct option:
qs.s: Monerans reproduce mainly asexually, lack a true nucleus, and are prokaryotes, making statements a, c, and d incorrect.

qs.q: Five kingdom system of classification suggested by R.H. Whittaker is not based on
o: Presence or absence of a well defined nucleus
qs.s: Presence/absence of a nuclear membrane, nutrition, and body complexity were main criteria; mode of reproduction was not a primary differentiator.

qs.q: Why are archaebacteria able to survive in extreme environments unlike other bacteria:
o: They are heterotrophic and depend on decaying organic matter.
They produce large amounts of biogas which helps them survive.
Their cell wall structure is fundamentally different, enabling adaptation to harsh conditions.
They undergo photosynthesis at very high temperatures
qs.s: A distinct cell wall structure without peptidoglycan enables archaebacteria to survive extreme conditions.

qs.q: Select the wrong statement :-
o: Bacterial cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan.
Pilli and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells.
qs.s: Pili and fimbriae function in surface attachment and conjugation, not in bacterial motility.

qs.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Bread mould - Ascomycetes
(II) Oospore - Sexual spore
(III) Chief oceanic producers - Diatoms
(IV) Red tide- Dinoflagellates
(V) Mixotrophic nutrition - Euglenoids
qs.s: Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct. Bread mould (Rhizopus) belongs to Phycomycetes.

qs.q:
Read the following pair:-
i. Diatoms-haploid body
ii. Dinoflagellates-water bloom
iii. Slime moulds-decomposer nature
iv. Euglenoids-some time behave like predator
v. Protozoa-Unicellular prokaryotes
Choose the correct option :-
qs.s: Pairs ii, iii, and iv are correct. Diatoms are diploid and protozoans are unicellular eukaryotes.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Morels and truffles are edible delicacies.
Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD.
Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously.
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae.
qs.s: Yeast is a unicellular fungus and lacks filamentous hyphal structures.

qs.q:
Which of the following are the characters of dinoflagellates?
(i) They are planktonic golden yellow algae with soap box like structure.
(ii) They are marine red biflagellated protists.
(iii) They appear yellow, green, brown, blue and red in colour.
(iv) They are biflagellated organisms with pellicle.
(v) They are saprophytic (or) parasitic unicellular forms.
qs.s: Dinoflagellates are primarily marine photosynthetic protists with two flagella displaying varied cellular pigmentation.

qs.q: Euglena, Nostoc, Chlorella, Mangifera Select the correct statement with respect to all these organisms:
o: All are photosynthetic and act as producers in nature.
Presence of chloroplast and cell wall.
qs.s: All four organisms are photosynthetic autotrophs that serve as primary producers.

qs.q: Virus envelope is known as
qs.s: The protective protein shell/coat enclosing viral nucleic acid is called a capsid.

qs.q:
Study the following statements and identify the correct ones:
(I) Diatoms float passively in water currents.
(II) Red tides are formed due to bioluminescence.
(III) Dinoflagellates are mostly fresh water organisms and photosynthetic.
(IV) Chrysophytes are found in freshwater as well as in marine environments.
qs.s: Statements I and IV are correct. Red tides are due to rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax, and dinoflagellates are mainly marine.

qs.q:
Match the following in relation to fungi.
A. Penicillium
B. Yeast
C. Puccinia
D. Trichoderma

P. Sexual reproduction absent
Q. Wheat rust fungus
R. Exogenous asexual spores and endogenous sexual spores
S. Budding
qs.s: Penicillium produces exogenous conidia and endogenous ascospores; Yeast reproduces by budding; Puccinia causes wheat rust; Trichoderma lacks sexual reproduction.

qs.q: Which of the following does not apply to ascomycetes?
o: Asexual spores called conidia are produced endogenously
qs.s: Ascomycetes have septate mycelium, are called sac fungi, and produce conidia exogenously; thus none of the options apply.

qs.q:
Select the incorrect statement with respect to dinoflagellates:
(I) These are golden-brown photosynthetic protists.
(II) They are mostly marine, and some are found in fresh water.
(III) They appear yellow, green, brown, blue, or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells.
(IV) Most of them are filamentous and lack flagella except in the reproductive stage.
qs.s: Dinoflagellates are unicellular and usually possess two flagella (one longitudinal, one transverse).

qs.q: The Cyanobacteria are also referred to as
qs.s: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic eubacteria commonly referred to as blue-green algae.

qs.q: Slime moulds and Unicellular algae are included in the kingdom protista because
o: Kingdom Protista includes eukaryotic organisms that do not clearly belong in the other three kingdoms
They lack important characteristics of the fungi and plants
They appear to be more closely related to unicellular eukaryotes
qs.s: Kingdom Protista acts as a group for unicellular eukaryotes that do not fit into Fungi, Plantae, or Animalia.

qs.q: The most abundant prokaryotes helpful to humans in making curd from milk and in production of antibiotics are the ones categorized as
qs.s: Heterotrophic bacteria like Lactobacillus (curd) and Actinomycetes (antibiotics) are widely utilized in human welfare.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is/are incorrect?
o: Under unfavourable conditions, bacteria produce spores
Bacteria reproduce by a sort of asexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of RNA transfer from one bacterium to other
qs.s: Bacteria reproduce primarily by binary fission and transfer DNA during primitive sexual reproduction, not RNA.

qs.q: Viruses are non-cellular organisms but replicate themselves once they infect the host cell. To which of the following kingdom do viruses belong to?
qs.s: Viruses are non-cellular entities and are not assigned to any kingdom in Whittaker's five-kingdom system.

qs.q: Difference between Virus and Viroid is
o: Absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus
Presence of low molecular weight RNA in virus but absent in viroid
qs.s: Viroids are naked RNA molecules lacking the capsid protein coat found in viruses.

qs.q: Why is a capsule advantageous to a bacterium?
o: It allows the bacterium to attach to the surface
It protects the bacterium from desiccation
It allows bacterium to hide from hosts immune system
qs.s: A thick mucilaginous capsule protects pathogenic bacteria from phagocytosis and host immune response.

qs.q: Which one single organism or pair of organism is correctly assigned to its or their taxonomic group?
o: Yeast used in making bread and beer in fungus
Nostoc and Anabaena are examples of protista
Lichen is a composite organism formed from the symbiotic association of an algae and a protozoan..
Paramecium and Plasmodium belong to the same kingdom as that of Penicillium.
qs.s: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Yeast) is a unicellular fungus belonging to Ascomycota.

qs.q: Which of the statement(s) given below is/are correct?
o: Kingdom-Protista forms a link between monerans and the other organisms like plants, animal and fungi
Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation
Being prokaryotic, the protistan cell body contains a well-defined nucleus and other membrane bound organelles
qs.s: Protista connects Monera with eukaryotes; protists are eukaryotic organisms, making statement 3 incorrect.

qs.q:
(I) Cholera
(II) Tetanus
(III) Plague
(IV) Turnip mosaic
(V) Citrus canker
(VI) Polio
Which of the following diseases mentioned above are caused by bacteria?
qs.s: Cholera, Tetanus, Plague, and Citrus canker are bacterial diseases, whereas Turnip mosaic and Polio are viral.

qs.q:
The following fungus belongs to class ascomycetes (count the total number).
Rhizopus, Penicillium, Neurospora, Yeast, Mucor, Agaricus, Toadstool, Albugo, Claviceps, Alternaria, Trichoderma, Aspergillus, Ustilago, Morels, Truffles, Colletotrichum, Puccinia
qs.s: Penicillium, Neurospora, Yeast, Claviceps, Aspergillus, Morels, and Truffles (7 total) belong to Ascomycetes.

qs.q: What is the role of heterocysts in a cyanobacterial filament?
o: They carry out photosynthesis and nitrogen fixation.
They oxidize inorganic substances to obtain energy.
They carry out only nitrogen fixation.
qs.s: Heterocysts are specialized thick-walled cells that carry out nitrogen fixation under anaerobic conditions.

qs.q:
Which of the following environmental conditions are essential for optimum growth of Mucor on a piece of bread?
A) Temperature of about 25°C
B) Temperature of about 5°C
C) Relative humidity of about 5%
D) Relative humidity of about 95%
E) A shady place
F) A brightly illuminated place
Choose the answer from the following options?
qs.s: Mucor requires warm (25°C), moist (95% humidity), and shady environment for optimal hyphal growth.

qs.q: Pigment-containing membranous extensions in some cyanobacteria are
qs.s: Chromatophores are internal membrane infoldings containing photosynthetic pigments in photosynthetic bacteria.

qs.q: When a fresh water protozoan is placed in marine water:
o: The contractile vacuole increases in size
A number of contractile vacuoles appear
qs.s: In hypertonic marine water, excess water loss occurs, eliminating the need for osmoregulatory contractile vacuoles.

qs.q: Consider the following statements, Which of the statements given below is incorrect?
o: All prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under kingdom-Archae
The unicellular eukaryotic organisms were placed in kingdom-Protista
Chlorella and Chlamydomonas, are placed in protista in 5- kingdom classification
Paramecium and Amoeba lack cell walls
qs.s: All prokaryotes were placed in Kingdom Monera, not Archaea.

qs.q: Black (stem) rust of wheat is caused by:
qs.s: Puccinia graminis tritici is a rust fungus that causes black stem rust of wheat.

qs.q: Thermococcus, Methanococcus, and Methanobacterium exemplify
o: Archaebacteria that contain protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
Archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively supercoiled
Bacteria that contain a cytoskeleton and ribosomes
Bacteria whose DNA relaxed or positively supercoiled but which have a cytoskeleton as well as mitochondria
qs.s: These Archaebacteria possess histone-like proteins homologous to eukaryotic core histones.

qs.q: Which is incorrect about phycomycetes?
o: A zygospore is formed by fusion of gametes
Asexual reproduction takes place by motile zoospores and non-motile aplanospores
White spots seen on mustard leaves are due to parasitic fungus Rhizopus
qs.s: White rust on mustard leaves is caused by the parasitic fungus Albugo candida, not Rhizopus.

qs.q: Select the wrong statement:
o: Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans
Cell wall is present in members of Fungi and Plantae
Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell in all kingdoms except Monera
qs.s: Sporozoans (e.g., Plasmodium) lack locomotory structures like pseudopodia, which are found in amoeboids.

qs.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?
o: Protistan body includes a well-defined nucleus, and no cellular organelles
Protists have nucleus along with flagella and cilia which doesnot confer motility
Protist cells have no nucleus but have some cellular organelles to perform basic functions
qs.s: Protists are eukaryotic organisms possessing a distinct nucleus, membrane-bound organelles, and functional locomotory cilia/flagella.

qs.q:
Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization.
A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin.
B. Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization.
C. Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids.
D. Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization.
E. Eukaryotes with cellular body organization.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
qs.s: The increasing structural complexity sequence is Monera (C) -> Protista (E) -> Fungi (A) -> Plantae (D) -> Animalia (B).

qs.q: After karyogamy followed by meiosis, spores are produced exogenously in
qs.s: Agaricus is a Basidiomycete which produces haploid basidiospores exogenously on basidia.

qs.q: What is incorrect for chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria :-
o: Oxidise various organic and inorganic substances
Uses the energy released through oxidation for their ATP production
Play great role in recycling of nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur
They are most abundant in nature
qs.s: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant bacteria in nature, not chemosynthetic autotrophs.

qs.q: Organisms living in salty areas are called as
qs.s: Halophiles are archaebacteria specifically adapted to hypersaline environments.

qs.q: Which one of the following is wrongly matched?
qs.s: Puccinia causes rust disease (wheat rust), whereas Ustilago causes smut.

qs.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Vibrio cholerae Cholera
(II) Salmonella typhi → typhoid
(III) Yeast Phycomycetes
(IV) Alternaria → Perfect fungi
qs.s: Statements I and II correctly match bacteria with diseases. Yeast is an Ascomycete and Alternaria is an imperfect fungus.

qs.q: Which of the statement(s) given below is/are correct for amoeboid protozoans?
o: Live in freshwater, sea water or moist soil
Has cilia for locomotion and capturing prey
Have silica shells on their surface in fresh forms
qs.s: Amoeboid protozoans live in freshwater, seawater, or moist soil and use pseudopodia for movement.

qs.q: The agents which are known to cause CJD are:
qs.s: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is caused by prions, which are abnormally folded infectious proteins.

qs.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Ascospore - Asexual spore
(II) Nitrosomonas - Nitrogen fixation
(III) Aspergillus niger- Produces acetic acid.
(IV) Saccharomyces cerevisiae-Ascomycetes.
qs.s: Saccharomyces cerevisiae belongs to Ascomycetes. Ascospores are sexual, Nitrosomonas oxidizes ammonia, and Aspergillus niger produces citric acid.

qs.q: Which one does not belong to Monera?
qs.s: Slime moulds are eukaryotic saprophytic protists classified under Kingdom Protista.

qs.q: Maximum nutritional diversity is found in the group
qs.s: Kingdom Monera exhibits extensive nutritional diversity (photoautotrophic, chemoautotrophic, saprophytic, and parasitic).

qs.q: Read the following statements and select incorrect statement.
o: Instead of the cell wall, euglenoids have a protein rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants
Toxins released by large number of red Dinoflagellates may even kill other marine animals such as fishes.
qs.s: All three given statements (1, 2, 3) are true, so none of them is incorrect.

qs.q: Which of the following microbes forms symbiotic association with plants and helps them in nutrition?
qs.s: Glomus species form endomycorrhizae with plant roots, assisting in nutrient (especially phosphorus) uptake.

qs.q: Which of the following organisms are known as chief producers in the oceans?
qs.s: Diatoms (chrysophytes) are microscopic photosynthetic plankton recognized as chief oceanic producers.

qs.q: Which of the following is a fungal disease?
qs.s: White spots on mustard (Albugo) and wheat rust (Puccinia) are fungal diseases.

qs.q:
The main difference between photosynthetic and chemosynthetic bacteria is that:
(I) Water is used by photosynthetic bacteria, whereas it is rejected by chemosynthetic bacteria.
(II) Photosynthetic bacteria are seen as parasites within green plant cells, whereas chemosynthetic bacteria are seen as saprophytes on decaying food substances.
(III) Photosynthetic bacteria include Nostoc, Anabaena, whereas chemosynthetic bacteria include Nitrosomonas.
(IV) Energy from sunlight is used in photosynthetic bacteria, while in chemosynthetic bacteria, energy is used by the oxidation of inorganic substances.
(V) Some photosynthetic bacteria are involved in nitrogen fixation, whereas chemosynthetic bacteria are involved in nitrification
qs.s: Statements III, IV, and V accurately distinguish photosynthetic and chemosynthetic bacteria.

qs.q:
The following characteristics are seen in which group of organisms?
(I) They are able to perform photosynthesis.
(II) Unicellular, colonial, filamentous, marine, or terrestrial forms.
(III) They often form blooms in water bodies.
(IV) The colonies are surrounded by a gelatinous sheath.
(V) Some can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts.
qs.s: Cyanobacteria are colonial/filamentous photosynthetic monerans with gelatinous sheaths and heterocysts.

qs.q:
Select the organism with loose tissue level body organisation from the box
i) Anabaena ii) Pseudomonas iii) Saccharomyces
iv) Agaricus v) Claviceps vi) Drosophila of Plant kingdom vii) Puff ball viii) Physarum ix) Gymnodium
qs.s: Fungi exhibit loose tissue (plectenchymatous) organization; Agaricus, Claviceps, Neurospora (vi), and Puffballs belong to fungi.

qs.q:
Select the correct answer about chrysophytes?
I. Found in fresh and marine water and are microscopic plankton
II. They are commonly called planktons and most of them are photosynthetic.
qs.s: Chrysophytes inhabit aquatic environments as microscopic plankton and are photosynthetic.

qs.q:
Select the correct answer - chrysophyta?
(i) They are saprophytic protists and they have a protein rich layer deposited with silica
(ii) They have indestructible wall layer deposited with silica and they are commonly called diatoms
qs.s: Chrysophytes include diatoms which possess cell walls embedded with indestructible silica.

qs.q:
Select the correct statement from the following for kingdom fungi
A. They are heterotrophic.
B. White spots seen on mustard leaves are due to a parasitic fungus.
C. Yeast is an multicellular fungus.
D. Fungi are filamentous.
qs.s: Statements A, B, and D are true. Yeast is unicellular, making statement C incorrect.

qs.q: Select the wrong statement:
o: Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans.
Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water.
The walls of diatoms are easily destructible.
'Diatomaceous earth' is formed by the cell walls of diatoms.
qs.s: Diatom cell walls are indestructible due to silica deposition.

qs.q:
Archaebacteria and Cyanobacteria are characterized by common features i.e
1. Rigid cell wall
2. Motile structure
3. cellular thallus organisation
4. Heterocyst for N₂ fixation
5. Mucilagenous sheath
6. Simple structure and complex in behaviour
qs.s: Both groups possess a rigid cell wall, simple cellular prokaryotic organization, and complex behavior.

qs.q: Select the mismatch:
qs.s: Rhodospirillum is a free-living photosynthetic purple non-sulfur bacterium, not a mycorrhizal fungus.

qs.q:
Which of the following are not considered in the five kingdom system of classification?
(I) Lichen
(II) Virus
(III) Viroid
(IV) Slime moulds
qs.s: Lichens, viruses, and viroids are excluded from Whittaker's five-kingdom classification.

qs.q: Contagium vivum fluidum was proposed by
qs.s: M.W. Beijerinck demonstrated infectious plant extracts and termed the fluid 'Contagium vivum fluidum'.

qs.q: Methanogens belong to :
qs.s: Methanogens are obligate anaerobic archaebacteria that produce methane.

qs.q: Which structures perform the function of mitochondria in bacteria ?
qs.s: Mesosomes are plasma membrane infoldings containing respiratory enzymes analogous to mitochondria.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is correct
qs.s: Euglenoids lack a cell wall and instead have a protein-rich flexible outer membrane called a pellicle.

qs.q: In the five-kingdom classification, Chlamydomonas and Chlorella have been included in
qs.s: Whittaker placed all unicellular eukaryotic algae (like Chlamydomonas and Chlorella) under Kingdom Protista.

qs.q: An example of endomycorrhiza is
qs.s: Glomus forms vesicular-arbuscular endomycorrhizae (VAM) with plant roots.

qs.q:
The following features belongs to
A. Body consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae.
B. Cell wall consist of chitin and polysaccharides
C. They prefer to grow in warm and humid places
qs.s: Hyphal filaments, chitinous cell walls, and preference for warm, humid habitats characterize Fungi.

qs.q: All eukaryotic unicellular organisms belong to
qs.s: Kingdom Protista includes all single-celled eukaryotic organisms.

qs.q:
Select the correct answer
I. Diatomaceous earth used as polishing, filtration of oils and filtration of syrup.
II. Chief 'consumers' in the oceans are diatoms.
qs.s: Statement I is correct. Diatoms are chief 'producers' (autotrophs) in oceans, not consumers.

qs.q: Identify the odd one out
qs.s: Ustilago is a Basidiomycete, while Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and Trichoderma are Deuteromycetes.

qs.q:
The characteristics mentioned below belong to:
(I) No asexual spores are generally formed.
(II) Mycelium is branched and septate.
(III) Vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common.
(IV) Sex organs are absent, but sexual reproduction takes place by somatogamy.
(V) Basidia are arranged in basidiocarp.
qs.s: Basidiomycetes (club fungi) lack sex organs/asexual spores and produce basidiospores on basidiocarps.

qs.q: In Eubacteria, a cellular component that resembles eukaryotic cell is
qs.s: The plasma membrane of eubacteria is structurally similar (lipid bilayer with proteins) to eukaryotic cell membranes.

qs.q: With respect to fungal sexual cycle, choose the correct sequence of events
qs.s: The sexual cycle in fungi follows: Plasmogamy (protoplasm fusion) -> Karyogamy (nuclear fusion) -> Meiosis.

qs.q:
Read the following features and identify the group of organisms they belong to:
(I) Body is septate and branched.
(II) They act as decomposers of litter.
(III) They reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia.
(IV) When their sexual forms were discovered, they were moved into the classes they rightly belong to.
qs.s: Deuteromycetes are imperfect fungi reproducing only via asexual conidia.

qs.q:
Match Column I with Column II.
Choose the correct answer from the option given below

Column I:
A. Saprophyte
B. Parasite
C. Lichens
D. Mycorrhiza

Column II:
P. Symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots
Q. Decomposition of dead organic materials
R. Living on living plants or animals
S. Symbiotic association of algae and fungi
qs.s: Saprophytes decompose dead matter; Parasites live on living hosts; Lichens are alga-fungus symbionts; Mycorrhizae are root-fungus symbionts.

qs.q: Which of the following statement is not true for Nostoc?
qs.s: Nostoc is a microscopic filamentous cyanobacterium (though colonies can be visible, individual organisms are microscopic).

qs.q: Membrane bound organelles are absent in
qs.s: Streptococcus is a prokaryotic bacterium and lacks membrane-bound cell organelles.

qs.q: Which of the following is odd?
qs.s: Alternaria belongs to Deuteromycetes, whereas Toadstool, Puccinia, and Mushroom belong to Basidiomycetes.

qs.q: The imperfect fungi which are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling belong to
qs.s: Deuteromycetes are decomposers of litter and aid in soil mineral cycling.

qs.q:
Karyogamy is delayed after Plasmogamy in the sexual life cycle of how many members?
Bread mould, Causal organism of wheat rust disease, puff ball, Drosophila of plant kingdom, Mushroom, Bracket fungi
qs.s: A delayed karyogamy (dikaryophase) occurs in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes (5 organisms: Puccinia, Puffball, Neurospora, Mushroom, Bracket fungi).

qs.q:
Characteristic feature of euglenoids are
A. Presence of pellicle
B. Presence of two flagella
C. Photosynthetic in presence of sunlight
D. Heterotrophic in absence of sunlight
qs.s: Euglenoids feature a flexible pellicle, two flagella, and mixotrophic nutrition (photosynthetic in light, heterotrophic in dark).

qs.q: Choose the wrong statement.
o: Marine amoeboid protozoan protists have silica shells
Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan protist
qs.s: Plasmodium is a sporozoan protozoan that does not possess a dikaryotic fungal-type body.

qs.q: Which one of the following matches is correct?
qs.s: Alternaria belongs to Deuteromycetes where sexual reproduction is absent/unknown.

qs.q: One of the major components of cell wall of most fungi is:
qs.s: Chitin (a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine) forms the rigid fungal cell wall.

qs.q:
Choose the features related to Cyanobacteria.
I. Symbionts in Cycas coralloid roots
II. Have mucilaginous sheath
III. Form blooms in polluted waters
IV. Have endospores
qs.s: Features I, II, and III apply to Cyanobacteria. Endospores are typical of specific eubacteria like Bacillus, not cyanobacteria.

qs.q: The bacteria present in the gut of several ruminant animals
o: Are similar to other bacteria in cell wall structure
Are anaerobes with peptidoglycan cell wall
Are responsible for production of biogas
qs.s: Methanogens present in cattle rumen convert cellulose derivatives into methane (biogas).

qs.q:
Find the incorrect statements from the following:
(I) Truffles - Club fungi
(II) Methanogens - Human intestine
(III) Thermoacidophiles - Hot sulphur springs
(IV) Slime moulds - True wall found in the vegetative stage.
(V) Whittaker's system of Classification brought together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella with Paramoecium, Amoeba in protista.
(VI) Roquefort cheese - Ascomycetes
qs.s: Truffles are sac fungi, Methanogens live in ruminant guts, and Slime mould spores (not vegetative stage) have true walls.

qs.q: Ciliates differ from all other protozoans in
o: having a contractile vacuole for removing excess water
qs.s: Ciliates (e.g., Paramecium) exhibit nuclear dimorphism, having a macronucleus (vegetative) and micronucleus (reproductive).

qs.q:
Study the following characters carefully and give answer:-
i. Bacterial structure is very simple because they are prokaryotic and unicellular
ii. Bacteria as a group show most extensive metabolic diversity
iii. Based on shape, bacteria are grouped into two categories only.
iv. Most of the bacteria do not have cell wall.
qs.s: Statements i and ii are correct. Bacteria are categorized into 4 shapes and mostly possess cell walls.

qs.q:
Select the correct answer
I. Chemosynthetic autotrophs bacteria oxidise various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia and use the released energy for their ATP production.
II. The organisms forming blooms in polluted water bodies are nutritionally Photosynthetic autotrophs.
qs.s: Both statements are correct; chemosynthetic bacteria oxidize inorganic matter for ATP, and water blooms are formed by photosynthetic cyanobacteria.

qs.q: Which of the following organisms in the list given below are autotrophs and perform oxygenic photosynthesis?
o: Anabaena, Sacharomyces, Green sulphur bacteria, Frankia
qs.s: Cyanobacteria (Nostoc, Anabaena, Oscillatoria) perform oxygenic photosynthesis using water as an electron donor.

qs.q:
Identify the organisms that produce their own food in kingdom Monera?
A. Algae
B. BGA
C. Cyanobacteria
D. Nitrifying bacteria
E. Mycoplasma
F. Nitrogen fixation bacteria
qs.s: Blue-green algae (BGA), Cyanobacteria, and Nitrifying bacteria are autotrophic monerans.

qs.q: Kingdom Monera includes
o: Unicellular and multicellular microorganisms with simplest metabolism
The most ancient microorganisms which are nutritionally heterotrophs only
Most ancient, the smallest, and most abundant microorganisms
qs.s: Monera includes the most ancient, primitive, abundant unicellular prokaryotic organisms.

qs.q: Identify the correct statement about three domains of life?
o: The three-domain system divides the Kingdom Monera into two domains
The three-domain system divides the Kingdom Monera into three domains
The three-domain system puts Kingdom Monera into first domain only
The three-domain system didnot include archaebacteria
qs.s: Carl Woese's three-domain system splits Kingdom Monera into Archaea and Bacteria domains.

qs.q: Sacharomyces, Albugo, Rhizopus, Ustilago, Puccinia, Agaricus, Trichoderma, Alternaria. Which of the following examples are belongs to class basidiomycetes.
qs.s: Ustilago (smut), Puccinia (rust), and Agaricus (mushroom) belong to Basidiomycetes.

qs.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Plasmodium Slime moulds Saprotrophic protists
(II) Experimental genetic Neurospora Ascomycetes
(III) Prions PSTD Protein
(IV) Edible fungi → Truffles and Morels → Ascomycetes
(V) Animal virus ssRNA HIV
qs.s: Statements I, II, IV, and V are correctly matched. PSTV is caused by viroids, not prions.

qs.q: Which of the following are found in extreme saline conditions?
qs.s: Halophilic archaebacteria inhabit extreme salty environments.

qs.q: Which of the following is correct statements?
o: Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, Ribosome and cell wall
Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
qs.s: Cyanobacteria are autotrophic prokaryotes belonging to Kingdom Monera.

qs.q:
Select the correct answer about slimemould spores
i. The spores possess true walls.
ii. They are extremely resistant and survive for many years, even under adverse conditions
iii. The spores are dispersed by water currents
qs.s: Statements i and ii are correct. Slime mould spores are dispersed by air currents, not water.

qs.q: Protista is similar to Plantae and different from Monera in having:
o: Protista and Plantae have a nuclear membrane.
Protista and Plantae are eukaryotes, whereas Monera are prokaryotes.
All Protista and Plantae are chlorophyll bearing and perform photosynthesis.
Protista and Plantae have a cellulosic cell wall.
qs.s: Protista and Plantae are both eukaryotic and possess a nuclear membrane.

qs.q: Which statement is wrong for viruses?
o: They have ability to synthesise nucleic acids and proteins.
Antibiotics have no effect on them.
All of them have helical symmetry.
qs.s: Viruses display cuboidal, helical, or complex/binal symmetry, not solely helical.

qs.q: Select the correct statement:-
o: Sporangiospores are exogenously produced in sporangium
In basidiomycetes asexual spores are generally not found.
Alternaria is a example of ascomycetes
qs.s: Asexual spores are generally not found in Basidiomycetes.

qs.q:
Which of the following is/are correct combinations with respect to their mycelium and mode of sexual reproduction:-
i. Albugo-Coenocytic mycelium and oogamy.
ii. Rhizopus- Aseptate mycelium and Isogamy.
iii. Puccinia - Septate mycelium and Anisogamy.
iv. Trichoderma - Aseptate mycelium and conidia formation
qs.s: Combinations i and ii correctly describe Phycomycete mycelium and sexual gamete fusion.

qs.q: Which one of the following also acts as a catalyst in a bacterial cell?
qs.s: 23S rRNA acts as peptidyl transferase (ribozyme) during bacterial protein synthesis.

qs.q: Which one of the following is true for fungi?
o: They lack a rigid cell wall
qs.s: Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms that mostly live as saprotrophs.

qs.q:
Which of the following are characteristics of members of Kingdom Protista?
i. Nucleus is present and DNA is associated with histone proteins.
ii. Cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S while organelle ribosomes are 70S.
iii. Members of the kingdom are heterotrophic with absorptive type of nutrition.
iv. Sap vacuoles are absent.
qs.s: Protists are eukaryotes with histone-bound DNA and eukaryotic (80S cytoplasm, 70S organellar) ribosomes.

qs.q:
Consider the statements
i. Organisms are known by only vegetative or asexual stage
ii. Most of the members are decomposers of litter
These statements are true for
qs.s: Deuteromycetes are imperfect fungi known only by vegetative/asexual stages and serve as litter decomposers.

qs.q:
What is the criteria used by Whittaker for classification?
(i) Cell structure
(ii) Body organisation
(iii) Mode of nutrition
(iv) Reproduction
(v) Phylogenetic relationship
(vi) Presence of mitochondria
(vii) Morphological character
o: i, ii, iii, iv, v, vi, vii
qs.s: Whittaker's main criteria were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

qs.q:
Identify the true (T) and false (F) statements w.r.t. diatoms
i. They are microscopic and float passively in water currents.
ii. Cell wall is made up of stiff cellulosic plates.
iii. Cell wall form two thin overlapping shells which fit together as in soap box.
iv. Cell wall is destructible and over few hundred years forms "diatomaceous earth"
o: i-F, ii-T, iii - T, iv - F
i-T, ii-T, iii - F, iv - F
qs.s: Statements i and iii are True. Statement ii is false (walls are siliceous) and iv is false (walls are indestructible).

qs.q: Nuclear membrane is absent in
qs.s: Nostoc is a prokaryotic cyanobacterium and lacks a nuclear membrane.

qs.q: Single celled eukaryotes are included in
qs.s: All single-celled eukaryotic organisms are grouped under Kingdom Protista.

qs.q: Consider the following statements about Ascomycetes. Which one of the statement given below is false?
o: They are saprophytic, decomposer, coprophilous and parasitic
Aspergillus, Claviceps, and Neurospora are important examples of Ascomycetes
qs.s: Ascomycetes have branched and septate mycelium, not coenocytic.

qs.q:
Match Column I with Column II
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Column I:
A. Rhizopus
B. Ustilago
C. Puccinia
D. Agaricus

Column II:
P. Mushroom
Q. Smut fungus
R. Bread mould
S. Rust fungus
qs.s: Rhizopus is bread mould, Ustilago is smut fungus, Puccinia is rust fungus, and Agaricus is mushroom.

qs.q:
Character belongs to slime moulds
A. Saprophytes
B. Forms plasmodium under unfavourable condition
C. Spores posses true walls
D. Spores are dispersed by water
E. Body moves along decaying twings and leaves engulfing organic matter.
qs.s: Plasmodium is formed under favorable conditions, and spores are dispersed by air currents.

qs.q: Select the correct statement..
o: Members of kingdom fungi show a great diversity in structures and habitat
Most fungi are saprophytic, some are parasites and some symbiotic
There are four classes under kingdom fungi
qs.s: All given statements accurately describe kingdom Fungi.

qs.q: In which group of organisms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells which fit together?
qs.s: Chrysophytes (diatoms) have overlapping siliceous cell wall shells fitting together like a soap box.

qs.q: Pick up the wrong statement
o: Cell wall is absent in Animalia.
Protists have photosynthetic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
Nuclear membrane is present in Monera.
qs.s: Monerans are prokaryotes and lack a nuclear membrane.

qs.q: Which of the following statement about Euglena is/are true?
o: The pigments of Euglena are quite different from those of green plants
qs.s: Euglenoids possess two flagella (one long, one short).

qs.q:
What is true regarding plasmids?
(I) Plasmids are used to monitor genetic transformation.
(II) Plasmids are present in bacterial cells.
(III) Plasmids are organisms with antibiotic resistance.
(IV) Plasmids are DNA molecules with Ori (origin of replication).
qs.s: Plasmids are extrachromosomal DNA molecules in bacteria containing Ori, used as genetic vectors (not individual organisms).

qs.q:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option, stating which one is true (T) and which one is false (F)?
i. Blue green algae are the photosynthetic monerans.
ii. Genetic material in eukaryotes is circular, double stranded, helical DNA not enclosed by nuclear envelope
iii. Sexual reproduction in Rhizopus is oogamous and the mode of sexual fusion is gametangial contact type.
iv. Noctiluca is the first dinoflagellate to show bioluminescence.
v. The fungal component of lichen is called phycobont and the algal component is called mycobiont.
o: i-T, ii-F, iii - F, iv-T, v - F
i-T, ii-F, iii - F, iv-T, v-T
i-T, ii-F, iii - T, iv - F, v-T
i-F, ii-F, iii - F, iv-T, v-F
qs.s: i and iv are True. Eukaryotes have linear DNA enclosed in a nucleus, Rhizopus shows isogamy, and fungal component is mycobiont.

qs.q:
The unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms with loose tissue level organisation shows
i. Diversity in habitat
ii. Diversity in morphology of mycelium
iii. Chitin in cell wall
iv. Degeneration of sex organs from lower to higher group
v. Optimum in growth in cool and humid places
o: i, ii, iii and v are correct
qs.s: Fungi grow optimally in warm and humid places, not cool places.

qs.q: Chrysophytes, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates and Slimemoulds are included in the kingdom
qs.s: All single-celled eukaryotic lineages belong to Kingdom Protista.

qs.q:
The following features belongs to class
A. Sexual spores produced endogenously.
B. Asexual spores conidia produced exogenously.
C. Many members of this class are edible.
qs.s: Ascomycetes produce endogenous ascospores, exogenous conidia, and include edible delicacies like morels and truffles.

qs.q:
Find the correct matching options from the following:
(I) Antibiotic source - Penicillium-Ascomycetes
(II) Paramecium - Ciliated protozoan - Two nuclei
(III) Trypanosoma - Flagellated protist Sleeping sickness
(IV) Viroids PSTD-DNA
(V) Yeast - Unicellular - Ascospore
qs.s: Statements I, II, III, and V are correct. Viroids cause PSTV and consist of free RNA, not DNA.
